Your Bibliography uses different citation styles: For one citation you only use the DOI, for some citations you use the arXiv Number and URL, and for some the DOI and URL.
You should either always provide a URL, or always provide a DOI. Using DOI has the advantage of having a standard URL with registered metadata that forwards you to the actual work. This makes citing easy, as you can use tools as https://www.doi2bib.org/ to find relevant metadata for your citation in the format the Exposé template uses. For literature that has no DOI (e.g. Mariane Hedegaard. “The zone of proximal development as basis for instruction), you can still use the URL and find the metadata for citing yourself.

You used "personalised" which is British English several times. Here you use "individualized" which is American English. For writing english text in general (not just academic text) decide on which English you want to use, and then aim to use it consistently. This helps your text and language skills to be perceived as more professional.
Besides some distinct vocabulary, British English is often easy to differentiate from American English by words ending on ise/ize.
The spelling with s is British English, the spelling with z is American English. Some British publications and dictionaries accept the z spelling as well, but it is always advisable to use consistent phrasing. As I assume you speak German, think of it as comparing Germany German to Austrian German. The differences are marginal, but if you intermix distinct terms of both languages, your text will loose professional sounding.
You may want to change this to "Anonymised", to match the British English in your title and text. (z vs. s)

It is always a good approach to cite existing recent literature that directly highlights the research gap that your work addresses within its text. This supports the claim of existence of an actual gap and underlines its importance within the context of current research.

HCI itself is not a framework, but a field of study that resulted in multiple theoretical frameworks (e.g. the interaction framework) that can be used to design the interaction between humans and computer systems. To not confuse the reader, clarify this, as it currently reads as if HCI is your used theoretical framework, when actually HCI is a field of study that resulted in several theoretical frameworks that are suitable for your work.
